candidate.answerReason: Reflecting B across the internal angle bisector produces a point B′ on AC with AB′ = 14. Then B′C = 5, N is the midpoint of BB′, and MN is a midsegment of triangle BCB′.

methods.label: Reflect across the angle bisector
methods.explanation:
The angle bisector and the perpendicular \(BN\) suggest reflecting \(B\) across \(AN\): this turns \(N\) into a midpoint, allowing us to use the given midpoint \(M\).

Let \(B'\) be the reflection of \(B\) across \(AN\). Because \(AN\) bisects the internal angle \(BAC\), reflection takes ray \(AB\) onto ray \(AC\). Reflection preserves length, so
\[
AB'=AB=14.
\]
Since \(AC=19\), the point \(B'\) lies between \(A\) and \(C\), and
\[
B'C=19-14=5.
\]
The reflection axis \(AN\) perpendicularly bisects \(BB'\). Since \(BN\perp AN\), the line \(BB'\) is precisely the line \(BN\), making \(N\) the midpoint of \(BB'\).

Now consider \(\triangle BCB'\). The points \(M\) and \(N\) are the midpoints of \(BC\) and \(BB'\), respectively. The segment joining two side midpoints has half the length of the third side. Therefore
\[
MN=\frac{B'C}{2}=\boxed{\frac52},
\]
which is choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
